items.reason: Verifier replies produce timestamped documents under the set's verify directory.
Each completed verification writes one report; fallback attempts share that report.
The contract keeps the verdict first; the report receives the following prose.
Verdict parsing stays unchanged, and malformed replies remain in the report.
PASS, FIXABLE, and NEEDS-HUMAN replies all produce reports.
PASS findings must name the evidence and explain each acceptance criterion.
Cache reads bypass report creation.
Invalidation deletes cached verdicts without deleting reports.
Previous reports stay outside Verifier prompts; human notes retain their existing path.
Human acceptance writes a report without invoking an agent.
The human report includes the rationale and the overridden non-PASS verdict.
The Accepted by header identifies human authorship.
Human reports use the same directory, filename format, facts, and latest-report reader.
The gate shows the latest report path and commit facts without its prose.
The paging entry opens the report and returns to the gate.
The set detail view includes the Verify report pointer.
Verify artifacts rank above Refine artifacts.
Agent prompt views gain no pointer; only Verifier response-contract goldens change.
Missing reports produce no preamble, paging entry, detail pointer, or artifact.
Badge and status derivation remain independent of report age.
Status rows retain truncated findings but gain no adjacent report pointer.
Both passes share rendering, filing, latest selection, and document-header reading.
The Refine paging error changes from “Could not read the refine report” to “Could not read the report.”
Refine prompt golden files are unchanged.

scores.rationale: The shared design and focused tests are good, but status-row pointers are missing and one Refine message changes.

accepted.behaviour: The one-line truncation of verification reasons stays where a status row has room for only one line, with the pointer to the full document beside it.
accepted.reason: The spec (spec.md:218-220) puts the report pointer beside the one-line findings in a status row. The Reference keeps the one-line findings but puts no pointer beside them. The spec wins; the Reference misses this behaviour.

accepted.behaviour: Refine's observable behaviour is unchanged: the same directory, the same filename stamps, the same header, and every surface it renders on looks exactly as before.
accepted.reason: The spec (spec.md:20-23, 56-57) says no Refine behaviour that a user can see changes. The Reference changes the Refine paging error from "Could not read the refine report" to "Could not read the report". The spec wins; the Reference misses this behaviour.
